harnessDefects.evidence: select is in aside#chat-threads (self/ui/pool-home/conversation-workspace.js:17-27); the rail starts closed, setThreads(viewState.threadsOpen ?? false) at :103; the app opens it through [data-open-model] (:104) or [data-toggle-thread-rail] (:105). Fresh requester had selectedId null, so the select was not hidden by :186; the catalog option was present and Ready (data-catalog attribute in the failure log).

harnessDefects.what: Multi-tab steps assume each same-context tab is an independent instance and requester; on the product route only one tab per browser profile can connect
harnessDefects.where: harness README line 36 and run-requester.mjs concurrency tabs (same context); run-contribution.mjs cachedOnly (second supplier tab) and competingTabs (two tabs, one context)
harnessDefects.evidence: probe bringup/probe-second-tab.json: second tab network.error "Another tab owns this peer connection", no consumer peer, no custody owner. Code: index.html product route boots /ui/pool-home/index.js and never calls ensureReploidWindowInstance (only kernel/boot.js:160 does), so getCurrentReploidInstanceId() is null without an instance URL parameter (self/instance.js:156-160) and storage is unscoped; self/host/work-swarm.js:165 calls peerOffers.acquire(); self/host/work-peer-offers.js:16-21 reads one stored peer id per room and takes Web Lock reploid:tool-peer:<id> with ifAvailable, rejecting the second tab.
harnessDefects.note: Whether one connected tab per profile is the intended product contract or a REP-7 concurrency defect is a product decision; the code path is deliberate (an explicit lock with a specific message).
